bill.name: Save Our Seas 2.0 Marine Debris Infrastructure Programs Reauthorization Act (S. 3022)
bill.status: Passed Senate without amendment by unanimous consent on 2025-11-19 · received in House and held at the desk on 2025-11-20
bill.analyzed: Full introduced-in-Senate bill (2 pages; §§1–2), with §2 as the sole substantive provision; the unchanged Senate-passed text and later disposition were checked separately

sourceLimits: The supplied 1,048-byte, 176-word raw source contains all substantive provisions of the introduced bill but is flattened, has no page boundaries or metadata sidecar, and omits the standard enacting clause visible in the official PDF. The matching official GovInfo introduced-version PDF establishes the two-page count. Congress.gov, not the supplied raw text, establishes the later status recorded above and shows that the Senate passed the same amendment without change. The bill amends 33 U.S.C. §4282(g)(1) and (2) by cross-reference without reproducing the programs, authorized amounts, eligibility rules, or grant purposes in those paragraphs. It extends an authorization of appropriations; it does not provide budget authority, require a later appropriation, compel an obligation or grant award, guarantee program operation, or state an environmental result. It also creates no performance target, reporting duty, resolution date, or recurring public data product. The goal below is therefore confined to the express authorization-date change. No defensible automatically resolvable series or empirical conditional was verified, so metrics and conditionals are empty and no series hints or stance matrices are supplied.

provisions.title: Section 2 — Reauthorization of EPA programs to combat plastic waste
provisions.heading: §2: Extend two EPA authorization-of-appropriations paragraphs through fiscal year 2030
provisions.quote: Section 302(g) of the Save Our Seas 2.0 Act ( 33 U.S.C. 4282(g) ) is amended, in each of paragraphs (1) and (2)— (1) by inserting in after described ; and (2) by striking 2025 and inserting 2030 .
provisions.context: Section 1 supplies only the short title. Section 2 is the bill's sole substantive provision. In each of paragraphs (1) and (2) of 33 U.S.C. §4282(g), it would insert the word “in” after “described” and replace the authorization end year 2025 with 2030. The date substitution would leave the rest of the two referenced authorization paragraphs unchanged. The word insertion is a grammatical correction, not a separate program or funding authority. The amendment would not itself appropriate funds, require EPA to make grants, change program eligibility or grant rules, or set a measurable environmental outcome. The Senate later passed the same text without amendment, but the measure has not been enacted. The bill supplies no performance target, reporting duty, or official data series from which to construct a mechanically resolvable forecast cell.
goals: Extend through fiscal year 2030 the authorization of appropriations for the EPA programs referenced in 33 U.S.C. §4282(g)(1) and (2).

effects.text: If enacted, replacing 2025 with 2030 in each paragraph would extend the existing authorization-of-appropriations period by five fiscal years, through fiscal year 2030, without changing the rest of the referenced authorization text.
Inserting “in” after “described” in each paragraph would correct the syntax of the two cross-references without creating a separate substantive authority.
The amendment would authorize possible future appropriations but would not itself supply budget authority, obligate funds, require grant awards, or determine program or environmental outcomes.

barriers.text: Even if the authorization is extended, actual funding and grant activity would depend on separate appropriations and program administration; the new end date alone supplies neither money nor a required level of activity.
